description: van't Hoff equilibrium plateau pressure model for metal hydride H2 storage
source: Lototskyy et al. (2014) Prog. Nat. Sci. Mater.; Sakintuna et al. (2007) Int. J. Hydrogen Energy

delta_H.note: Enthalpy of hydride formation (absorption, exothermic, negative). Sandrock (1999) J. Alloys Compounds: LaNi5 dH = -30.1 kJ/mol

delta_S.note: Entropy of hydride formation (absorption, negative). Sandrock (1999): LaNi5 dS = -108 J/mol/K. Dominated by H2 gas entropy (~-130 J/mol/K at STP)

H_max_wt_pct.note: Maximum gravimetric H2 capacity for LaNi5. Sakintuna et al. 2007

volumetric_capacity.note: Volumetric H2 capacity for LaNi5 hydride. DOE targets: 40 g/L = 40 kg/m3

bed_volume_m3.note: Reference bed volume for 10 kg LaNi5 bed at ~4000 kg/m3 bulk density (powder bed with 50% packing). Gives ~56 kg_H2/m3 volumetric capacity.

hysteresis_factor.note: Absorption plateau pressure = hysteresis_factor * desorption plateau pressure. Lototskyy et al. 2014

plateau_slope_factor.note: Slope factor s in ln(P) = s*(x - 0.5) + ln(P_eq) for sloped plateau. Set 0 for flat.

cp_hydride.note: Heat capacity of LaNi5H6 hydride. Herbst & Hector 2005
